lines.text: Do you know how a photo can give away where you live? It's not the picture. It's hidden notes inside the file.
Every time you take a photo, your phone writes extra data into the file, called metadata. The time, the phone model, the camera settings.
And if location is on, the exact GPS coordinates, often accurate to a few metres.
Anyone with the original file can read it in seconds. Drop the numbers into a map, and there's your front door.
Many social apps remove this data when you post. But send the original file, and the notes usually go with it.
You can turn off location for your camera, or remove it before you share.
Orbi is just as careful with where you are. Other people only ever see a rough area, about forty kilometres wide. And in Anonymous mode, it doesn't use GPS at all.
